subject.title: Feature Request: Abstract file scanning pipeline as Memory Plugin API

question: Should OpenClaw add a public host-delivered memory file-ingestion API for active memory plugins, or keep file scanning owned by each memory backend/plugin?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent SDK shape and local-file trust boundary decide what local files third-party plugins may receive and therefore require maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a narrow SDK design first
options.body: Design and approve a minimal memory ingestion capability with explicit security, compatibility, and test requirements before implementation.

options.title: Keep scanning plugin-owned
options.body: Document that memory plugins may use current list/read helpers but must own watchers, indexing, deletion, and cleanup behavior themselves.

options.title: Fold into broader backend design
options.body: Defer this issue until a broader memory backend/provider contract also decides file ingestion, search, get, writeback, and status ownership.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow SDK design first
recommendation.body: Design and approve a minimal memory ingestion capability with explicit security, compatibility, and test requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history around the memory host SDK extraction and plugin-boundary design that this decision would extend.
